title: kblog.py proposes LOG rows from the ops store
goal: kblog.py propose --since DAY derives aggregates (counts, medians, ranges) from the ops sidecar's rows as proposed LOG rows, each with its source run ids, its observed date range and the context it relates to; it writes no raw event, person or text; a second run proposes nothing new.

gates.question: This adds a mechanism before a failure it answers has happened (backlog.md, Changing this process). Add it anyway?
Which aggregates does kblog.py propose make from the ops sidecar's rows?
options: one row per event and context: row count, nonzero-exit count, ms median and range
one row per aggregate (count, median and range each its own row)
gates.recommendation: one row per event and context: row count, nonzero-exit count, ms median and range
gates.answer: one row per event and context: row count, nonzero-exit count, ms median and range

gates.question: What context does a proposed row carry for an ops event that names no item (sync.gate, test.run, ci.pipeline, intake.detect)?
options: the item or sprint the event names; an event with none is left out unless --context names one
never aggregate events with no item
gates.recommendation: the item or sprint the event names; an event with none is left out unless --context names one
gates.answer: the item or sprint the event names; an event with none is left out unless --context names one
